text:
maria: Hey team — noticed a 2.3x CPU spike on host preprocessing for streaming requests after yesterday's deploy. Flamegraph attached: https://ci.redwood/fg/1758002999

owen: saw that in the dashboard too. spike correlates with small-chunk streaming (clients sending 8-32 token chunks).

alec: quick summary from my profiling run: host-side tokenization + JSON parse is ~45% of the extra wall time, while stream framing + per-chunk HTTP header construction is ~30%. KV cache misses account for most of the remaining tail.

maria: suspecting two things: our tokenizer allocations per chunk and per-request parsing creating new buffers. also gRPC path is hitting message boundary copies.

jana: can you paste the flamegraph snippet?

maria: pasted key stack here:
```
host_preproc                    45%\n  Tokenizer::encode_batch       28%\n    std::string::append         12%\n    VocabLookup::apply          10%\n  RequestParser::parse_stream   17%\n    json::parse                 11%\n    ChunkFramer::frame_payload  6%\n```

owen: interesting that `encode_batch` dominates. we're allocating per chunk instead of reusing a buffer. I tried a quick patch to pool string buffers in host prep and saw ~18% CPU reduction locally.

alec: what about the gRPC vs HTTP split? metrics?

maria: HTTP/1.1 endpoints worse on small chunks: each chunk does header formatting + writev -> syscall. gRPC path does protobuf encode + flush, less syscall overhead but we still copy payload into a gRPC-owned buffer.

ci-bot: Build #8273: perf/regression check — streaming latency 95p increased by 30% on service-host-preproc after commit a1b2c3.

jana: KV cache behavior note: when cache miss rate rises (seen with many short prompts), we re-load full KV segments which causes CPU + memory churn. For short streams that only need prefix tokens, we could consider partial KV lookup (lazy fill).

owen: proposal: three PRs — 1) buffer pool for tokenizer + reuse of token id vector, 2) batch small incoming stream chunks server-side (coalesce up to 128 tokens or 50ms), 3) incremental KV lookup to avoid rehydrating entire KV pages for tiny prefixes.

alec: agree. small coalescing window is key — too long hurts client latency. suggest heuristic: if chunk < 32 tokens and inter-arrival < 40ms, coalesce. otherwise flush. Add metric toggles to A/B.

maria: I prototyped buffer pool — microbench: `Tokenizer::encode_batch` went from 2.1ms -> 1.6ms for 16-token inputs (24% improvement). memory allocs dropped ~70%. patch here: https://phab/DE/1234

nowen: for copying on writev and gRPC, we should switch to scatter/gather where possible and avoid intermediate string formatting for headers. Also keepalive and connection reuse metrics show higher overhead for short-lived HTTP requests; prefer HTTP/2 or gRPC for streaming where we can.

alec: agree on HTTP/2. Add a server-side option to prefer gRPC over HTTP for streaming routes when client supports it. fallback remains.

jana: about KV: lazy prefix lookup needs careful TTL/eviction semantics. if we partial-fill, we must ensure cache coherence when model switches or kv pages are evicted. Also need to add instrumentation for partial-hit ratio.

maria: action items: (1) maria/owen — land buffer pool + tokenizer reuse (canary on dev), (2) owen — implement coalescing heuristic and expose as config, (3) jana — design lazy KV partial fills + metrics, (4) alec — add prefer-gRPC flag and add perf test.

maria: timeline: aim to land all 4 small PRs in the next sprint. I'll open the task board after this thread.

sre-bot: Incident ticket #INF-492 opened for elevated host-preproc CPU. Assigned to eng-runtime.

nowen: quick note — rolling canary necessary, since this changes allocation patterns and framing. I'll set up 10% canary with trace sampling.

alec: let's also add a perf job that simulates many small-chunk streams (8-32 token churn) to catch regressions next time.

maria: thanks all. ping me if you want to pair on the buffer pool design. :thumbsup:
